function.name: get_weather_forecast
function.description: Retrieves the weather forecast for a specified location and date range. The forecast includes temperature, precipitation, and wind speed. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: The location for which the weather forecast is requested, in the format of 'City, Country' (e.g., 'London, UK').

start_date.description: The start date of the period for the weather forecast in the ISO 8601 format (e.g., '2023-04-01').

end_date.description: The end date of the period for the weather forecast in the ISO 8601 format (e.g., '2023-04-07').

units.description: The unit system in which to return the weather forecast data.

include_details.description: Specifies whether to include detailed forecast information such as humidity and visibility.

### 1.  What Turbonomics is and why it matters for a multi‑cloud environment

| Feature | Turbonomics (AIOps platform) | Native Cloud AIOps / Observability tools |
|---------|------------------------------|------------------------------------------|
| **Scope** | Works **across all clouds** (AWS, Azure, GCP, on‑prem, edge) in a single pane of glass | Each provider offers its own set of services that are tightly coupled to that provider’s ecosystem |
| **Data ingestion** | Pulls telemetry from **any source** – cloud APIs, Kubernetes, OpenTelemetry, Prometheus, logs, metrics, events, even custom data | Usually limited to the provider’s own monitoring stack (e.g., CloudWatch, Stackdriver, Monitor) |
| **AI/ML engine** | Uses a **single, continuously learning model** that normalises data, detects anomalies, predicts capacity, and recommends actions across clouds | Each provider has its own ML models but they are siloed; you need to stitch them together manually |
| **Automation** | Executes **policy‑driven automation** (auto‑scale, auto‑re‑allocate, auto‑re‑balance, auto‑re‑configure) across clouds | Automation is provider‑specific (e.g., AWS Auto Scaling, Azure Autoscale, GCP Managed Instance Groups) |
| **Cost optimisation** | Provides a unified cost‑visibility layer and optimisation recommendations that span all clouds | Cost dashboards are provider‑specific; cross‑cloud cost optimisation requires third‑party tools |
| **Governance & compliance** | Centralised policy engine that enforces compliance across all clouds | Policies are enforced per‑cloud; cross‑cloud governance is fragmented |
| **Integration** | Integrates with CI/CD, incident‑management (PagerDuty, ServiceNow), chatops, and custom dashboards | Integration is usually limited to the provider’s native ecosystem or requires custom connectors |

---

### 2.  How Turbonomics can help Unilever

| Business goal | Turbonomics capability | Practical outcome for Unilever |
|---------------|------------------------|--------------------------------|
| **Unified observability** | Single‑pane dashboard that aggregates metrics, logs, events, and traces from AWS, Azure, GCP, and on‑prem | Unilever’s ops teams see one view of performance, latency, errors, and resource utilisation, eliminating “cloud‑centric blind spots” |
| **AI‑driven anomaly detection** | Continuous learning model that flags outliers before they become incidents | Faster incident response, reduced MTTR, and proactive remediation of performance regressions |
| **Predictive capacity planning** | Forecasts future load and recommends right‑size resources | Avoid over‑provisioning (cost savings) and under‑provisioning (performance degradation) across all sites |
| **Automated remediation** | Policy‑driven actions (e.g., spin‑up new instances, shift workloads, change instance types) | Self‑healing infrastructure that keeps services running without manual intervention |
| **Cross‑cloud cost optimisation** | Unified cost‑visibility and optimisation engine that suggests cheaper instance types, spot usage, or rightsizing | Real‑time cost savings, better budget adherence, and clearer ROI on cloud spend |
| **Governance & compliance** | Centralised policy engine that enforces SLAs, security, and regulatory requirements | Consistent compliance across all regions and clouds, easier audit trails |
| **DevOps acceleration** | Integrates with CI/CD pipelines, chatops, and incident‑management tools | Faster release cycles, fewer production incidents, and smoother collaboration between dev and ops |

---

### 3.  Key differences from native cloud tools

| Aspect | Turbonomics | GCP native tools | AWS native tools | Azure native tools |
|--------|-------------|------------------|------------------|--------------------|
| **Multi‑cloud coverage** | Yes – single platform | No – GCP‑only | No – AWS‑only | No – Azure‑only |
| **Unified AI model** | One model that learns across clouds | Separate models per service | Separate models per service | Separate models per service |
| **Automation scope** | Cross‑cloud policy‑driven automation | Cloud‑specific automation (e.g., Cloud Functions, Cloud Run) | Cloud‑specific automation (e.g., Lambda, Auto Scaling) | Cloud‑specific automation (e.g., Azure Functions, VM Scale Sets) |
| **Cost optimisation** | Unified cost‑visibility + optimisation | GCP Cost Management | AWS Cost Explorer | Azure Cost Management |
| **Observability stack** | Aggregates metrics, logs, traces, events from all sources | Stackdriver (now Cloud Monitoring, Logging, Trace) | CloudWatch, X-Ray, CloudTrail | Monitor, Log Analytics, Application Insights |
| **Integration ecosystem** | Connects to any CI/CD, chatops, incident‑management | GCP‑centric integrations | AWS‑centric integrations | Azure‑centric integrations |
| **Governance** | Centralised policy engine | GCP IAM & Policy Controls | AWS IAM & Service Control Policies | Azure RBAC & Policy |

---

### 4.  Bottom line for Unilever

- **Single pane of glass**: Turbonomics gives Unilever one dashboard that spans all its cloud environments, eliminating the need to switch between GCP, AWS, Azure, and on‑prem dashboards.
- **AI‑first**: The platform’s AI engine learns from all telemetry, providing consistent anomaly detection, predictive capacity planning, and automated remediation across clouds.
- **Cost & governance**: Unified cost optimisation and policy enforcement help Unilever keep spending in check while meeting regulatory and security requirements.
- **Speed & reliability**: By automating remediation and scaling decisions, Unilever can reduce MTTR, improve uptime, and accelerate time‑to‑market for new features.

In short, Turbonomics turns a fragmented, cloud‑centric observability stack into a cohesive, AI‑driven operating model that can scale with Unilever’s global, multi‑cloud footprint.
